Architecture.description:
The direction dependencies are allowed to point. `layers` is ordered inner to outer, and a file may import its own layer and any layer before it — so the domain cannot reach for an adapter, whatever the import graph would otherwise allow.

Silent until a project declares it: an architecture nobody stated is not one rqx should invent.

layers.description: Layer names, ordered inner to outer. A file may import its own layer and any layer before it.

paths.description: Glob to what it belongs to. A sub-table because `flatten` and `deny_unknown_fields` cannot both apply to one struct, and losing the typo check would cost more than the extra line of YAML.

layer.description: The layer this subtree belongs to; it must be named in `architecture.layers`.

may_not_import.description: Globs this subtree may not import from.

may_only_import.description: The only globs this subtree may import from.

BaselineMatch.description: How many findings one baseline entry covers.

Category.description: The top-level organisation, because eight axes are what a reader can hold in their head where sixty rules are not.

oneOf.description: Text that costs a reader and buys nothing.
Work that grows faster than the data it runs on.
Findings other tools reported, read from their SARIF output. No rule in the catalogue belongs to it, so it is not part of `ALL`, and the health score does not count it.

Comment.description: What `rqx comment` writes into the merge request.

mention_owners.description: Write the owners of files with new findings as real `@mentions`, which the forge notifies. Off by default: the names are written inside code spans, which it does not.

CostEntry.description: One user-written line of the library cost table.

fn.description: A free function, such as `std::find`, in place of `receiver` and `method`.

id.description: A name for the entry, unique among the entries of the project.

method.description: The method name, for an entry that names a receiver.

pure.description: The call has no side effects, so repeating it with the same arguments in a loop is repeated work.

receiver.description: Types the method belongs to, such as `[Array, "T[]"]`.

size_of.description: Where the size comes from when it is not the receiver, such as `arg0.receiver`.

space.description: Extra space, in the same notation. Defaults to constant.

when.description: Conditions on the arguments, such as `{arg0: literal 0}`.

CustomRule.description: A rule written as a tree-sitter query. The query is not compiled here — core has no grammars — but every other field is checked the moment the config parses.

confidence.description: Defaults to `verified`: a query either matched or it did not.

family.description: The family the rule is filed under.

hint.description: What to do about it, shown beside the finding.

id.description: The rule's slug, used to disable it and to waive it.

query.description: A tree-sitter query. Name the capture to report `@site`; without one the first capture is used.

severity.description: Defaults to `warning`.

Entrypoints.description: Modules the project is entered through. Anything reachable from one is live by definition, so these are read before an export is called unused.

paths.description: Globs of the modules the project is entered through.

Fix.description: Which mechanical fixes `rqx fix` may apply. A project that keeps commented-out code as documentation should not have it deleted, and naming the rule here beats remembering a flag per run.

apply.description: Autofix kinds, or individual rule slugs. Empty applies every kind.

disabled.description: Fixes to leave alone even when their kind is applied: kinds or rule slugs.

max_rounds.description: One fix can make the next possible, so fixing repeats. A cap rather than a fixed point, because a rule pair that undid each other would never settle.

min_confidence.description: The lowest finding confidence whose fix is applied. `verified` by default; `low` applies every mechanical fix, as rqx 0.5.0 did.

Gate.description: What makes `rqx check` fail. Defaults are deliberately permissive: a gate that fails on day one gets disabled on day one, and a disabled gate checks nothing.

baseline.description: Where the recorded debt lives. When it is set, only findings the baseline does not already hold count against `fail_on` and `max_findings` — which is what lets a codebase with ten years of history turn the gate on at all. `min_health` and `min_grade` still see everything.

baseline_match.description: How a scan's findings are matched against the baseline's entries. `count`: an entry covers as many findings with its identity as the baseline recorded, and any beyond that count are new. `set`: an entry covers every finding with its identity, however many there are, which is how rqx 0.5.0 and earlier matched.

complexity_regression.description: What a function whose time order grew against the base revision does to the verdict of `rqx check`: nothing (`off`), a report that does not fail the run (`warning`), or a failure (`error`). Anything but `off` also makes `rqx check` and `rqx comment` compare against the base revision, which `--regressions` does for one run.

fail_on.description: Lowest severity that counts against the gate.

fail_on_incomplete.description: Fail on a design pattern that is half applied. Off by default and the only way advice reaches an exit code: a pattern that would merely fit is not a defect, and turning this on for everyone would change what every existing pipeline returns.

max_findings.description: Findings allowed in the reviewed set before the check fails.

min_grade.description: Lowest grade any single file may carry. Catches a file rotting on its own, which a project-wide score averages away.

min_health.description: Health score below which the check fails; 0 disables the score gate.

owners.description: A floor per owner, keyed by the owner as CODEOWNERS writes it, for the files that owner answers for. Needs a CODEOWNERS file; the verdict names each owner that fell short.

ratchet.description: Fail when the total number of findings is above what the baseline recorded. A baseline says which debt is tolerated; this says it may not grow.

patterns.description: Globs of files rqx does not read, matched against paths relative to the scanned directory.

Language.description: The languages Rqx can analyze. A finding carries one so that a rule which cannot exist in a language is a declared exemption rather than a silent absence.

oneOf.description: Spelled out, because kebab-case would make it `type-script` in `rqx.yaml` while `rqx rules --language` takes the slug — one name, two spellings. The same goes for `JavaScript`.
Last, so the order the other languages were added in — which the clone salt and the per-language counters are built on — does not move.

Languages.description: Which languages a scan reads. Empty means all of them: a project that only holds one language pays nothing for the others, because the file walker never yields a path no language claims.

enabled.description: Language names. Empty means all six.

Level.description: How much a project asks of itself. A level is a layer of settings merged *under* everything written by hand, so naming one changes the defaults and never overrides a value the project stated.

Locked.description: Keys a policy forbids a project to change, as `table.key`.

keys.description: Keys, as `table.key`, that a project may not set to a different value.

OwnerGate.description: What one owner's files must meet. Both checks are off until set, so an entry names only the floor its owner has agreed to.

fail_on.description: Lowest severity that fails the check when the owner's files hold a finding of it, ignoring findings a baseline already records.

min_health.description: Health score of the owner's files below which the check fails; 0 disables it.

Patterns.description: Addressable four ways because the useful question differs: by advisory when one claim is wrong for this project, by pattern when the whole pattern is, by family, and by stance when a project wants the half-applied patterns and not the suggestions.

disabled.description: Advisory slugs, pattern slugs or families to switch off.

enabled.description: Advisories that ship off, switched on by advisory, pattern or family.

families.description: When non-empty, only these families run.

stances.description: When non-empty, only these stances are reported.

Performance.description: Client names and call names the I/O rules should recognise on top of the ones rqx ships, and the cost of library calls the cost tables do not know. Added to the built-in vocabulary rather than replacing it, because a project that names its own gateway still has a `fetch` somewhere.

costs.description: How much a library call costs, for the calls the built-in cost tables do not list. Each entry names a call by `receiver` and `method`, or by `fn`, and gives its time as `cost`: `1`, `log n`, `n`, `n log n`, `n^2` or `n*m`, where `n` is the size of the receiver and `m` the size of the first argument. Entries are read by the cost analysis and are part of the cache key; no report shows its result yet.

max_order.description: The largest time order a reviewed function may have, such as `O(n log n)`. Unset means no limit. A function in the reviewed files above it fails the run.

methods.description: Call names the I/O rules should recognise, one segment each.

receivers.description: Client names the I/O rules should recognise, one segment each.

RegressionGate.description: Whether, and how loudly, a complexity regression counts against the gate.

Scan.description: `prune_dirs` exists separately from `Ignore::patterns` because a glob still requires descending into a directory to produce the paths it then rejects, which on a populated `node_modules` is the difference between skipping a directory and walking every file in it.

cache.description: Reuse `.rqx/cache.bin` for files whose contents have not changed. It was off because a warm run was no faster than a cold one, but that was measured while the collector joined the git thread before draining the channel: the wait, not the parsing, was what a cache could not beat. With that gone a warm scan of 3,440 files costs 298ms against 2,023ms cold.

churn_days.description: Days of git history to read for churn; 0 turns the signal off.

coverage.description: Coverage files to read, so a test run can contradict a dead-code finding.

max_filesize.description: Bytes. A larger file is reported as skipped.

max_findings.description: How many findings the report shows. 0 shows every one. Never moves the score.

profile.description: CPU profiles to read, so a run can say which performance findings are on a path that executes.

respect_gitattributes.description: Skip files that `.gitattributes` marks `linguist-generated` or `linguist-vendored`, and list them as skipped. The file at the scanned directory and the one at the repository root are read.

sarif_in.description: SARIF 2.1.0 files other tools wrote. Their results become findings in the `external` family, under rule ids prefixed with the tool's name.

skip_generated.description: Skip files carrying a generator's marker, and list them as skipped.

skip_minified.description: Skip files that read as minified, and list them as skipped. Only a file whose non-blank lines are at least half over 300 characters can be: then a line over 4,000 characters with lines over 1,000 holding at least 80% of the file, lines that average over 300 characters across at least 5, or over 1,000 across fewer.

skip_submodules.description: Which git submodules listed in `.gitmodules` to leave out, each reported as skipped. `auto` leaves out those hosted under another organisation than the project's `origin`, `all` leaves out every one, `none` scans them all.

threads.description: Worker threads. 0 lets rqx pick from the machine.

SubmodulePolicy.description: Which git submodules a scan leaves out.

oneOf.description: Leave out a submodule whose URL names another host or organisation than the project's `origin` remote. A relative URL, or a project with no `origin`, counts as the project's own.
Scan every submodule as the project's own code.

SubtreeOverride.description: What a subtree may say differently. Only thresholds, rules and patterns, because the walker is built once and the gate reaches one verdict: honouring a scoped `scan` would mean walking the tree twice.

level.description: A subtree can be held to a different level: strict in the domain, relaxed in the scripts. The gate is not moved by it.

paths.description: Globs, relative to the directory of the file that wrote them.

patterns.description: Pattern advice switches for this subtree, merged over the project's.

rules.description: Rule switches for this subtree, merged over the project's.

thresholds.description: Thresholds for this subtree, merged over the project's.

Thresholds.description: Every threshold is the highest acceptable value: a finding fires strictly above it. Mixing `>` and `>=` across rules makes a configured number mean different things depending on which rule reads it.

boundary_repeats.description: Times the same off-by-one boundary arithmetic may repeat. Tunes `boundary-arithmetic`.

callback_depth.description: Function literals nested inside other function literals. Tunes `callback-nesting`.

class_collaborators.description: Other classes one class may depend on. Tunes `many-collaborators`.

class_members.description: Members one class may declare. Tunes `large-class`.

class_public_members.description: Public members one class may expose. Tunes `wide-surface`.

class_statements.description: Statements across all the methods of one class. Tunes `large-class`.

clone_min_nodes.description: Tunes `duplicate-code` and `reimplemented-existing`. A floor on AST nodes rather than statements, to reject a block of three bare identifiers. Statement count is the primary filter: candidates are only taken at extractable block boundaries, where a real three-statement block runs to roughly twenty nodes.

clone_min_statements.description: Smallest repeated block, in statements, that is reported as duplicate code or as a function that repeats an existing one. Tunes `duplicate-code` and `reimplemented-existing`.

cognitive_complexity.description: Cognitive complexity of one function, which counts nesting as well as branches. Tunes `cognitive-complexity`.

commented_code_lines.description: Consecutive lines of commented-out code. Tunes `commented-out-code`.

condition_operands.description: Operands in one boolean condition. Tunes `complex-condition`.

configuration_depth.description: Block nesting at which a configuration literal counts as buried. Tunes `buried-configuration`.

cyclomatic_complexity.description: Independent paths through one function. Tunes `cyclomatic-complexity`.

data_clump_sites.description: Functions that must share the same group of parameters before it is a data clump. Tunes `data-clump`.

data_clump_size.description: Parameters that travel together before they are a data clump. Tunes `data-clump`.

declaration_distance_lines.description: Lines a reader must hold a binding in mind before its first use is too far. Tunes `distant-declaration`.

explanation_ratio.description: How many times longer than the code it describes a comment may be. Tunes `explanation-longer-than-code`.

expression_operations.description: Operations packed into one unnamed expression before it stops being readable. Tunes `obscured-expression`.

fan_in.description: Modules that may import one file. Tunes `wide-fan-in`.

fan_out.description: Modules one file may import. Tunes `wide-fan-out`.

feature_envy_ratio.description: How many times more a method uses another class's members than its own. Tunes `feature-envy`.

function_locals.description: Local variables one function may declare. Tunes `many-locals`.

guard_cascade.description: Guard clauses stacked at the top of one function. Tunes `guard-cascade`.

hotspot_commits.description: Commits to one file within `scan.churn_days` before it is a hotspot. Tunes `hotspot`.

inheritance_depth.description: Levels of inheritance above one class. Tunes `deep-inheritance`.

log_percent.description: Percentage of a function's statements that are logging. Tunes `over-logging`.

loop_nesting.description: Loops inside loops before the body's cost is a power of the input. Tunes `deep-loop-nesting`.

magic_number_repeats.description: Times one unnamed number may repeat before it wants a name. Tunes `magic-number`.

max_cases.description: Arms in one switch before it stops being a table a reader scans. Tunes `wide-switch`.

max_exits.description: Ways out of one function body, past the guard clauses at the top. Tunes `many-exits`.

max_params.description: Parameters one function may take. Tunes `long-parameter-list`.

max_results.description: Results one function may return. Tunes `many-results`.

message_chain_depth.description: Calls chained on one object before the chain reaches too far. Tunes `message-chain`.

min_cases.description: Arms below which a switch is an if spelled in more lines. Tunes `tiny-switch`, which is off by default.

module_statements.description: Statements in one file across all its functions. Tunes `oversized-module`.

narrated_run.description: Consecutive lines each narrated by its own comment. Tunes `comment-per-line`.

nesting_depth.description: Levels of nested control flow in one function. Tunes `deep-nesting`.

relative_climb.description: Levels a relative import may climb. Tunes `deep-relative-import`.

short_name_scope_lines.description: Lines a short name may stay in scope. Tunes `short-name-wide-scope`.

slow_test_ms.description: Milliseconds a test may pause: a longer pause is wall clock on every run. Tunes `slow-test`.

sole_author_commits.description: Commits by one author, and no one else, before a file counts as single-author. Tunes `single-author-file`.

test_decisions.description: Decisions one test body may make before it is reported. An `if` that only fails the test and a loop over a table of cases are not counted. Tunes `branching-test`.

todo_age_days.description: Days a TODO may stand before it is stale. Tunes `stale-todo`.

try_statements.description: Statements inside one try block. Tunes `wide-try`.

Update.description: Whether rqx may ask GitHub if a newer release exists. The check runs on a thread nobody waits for, caches its answer for a day, and never runs in CI — but a tool that reaches the network at all should be answerable to a line in a config file.

check.description: Ask GitHub whether a newer release exists.

extends.description: Settings this file builds on, merged under its own keys, later entries over earlier ones. Each is a built-in preset (`recommended`, `strict`, `legacy-adoption`, `ci-gate`, `perf`, or a level name) or a path to another YAML file, relative to this one. Read by the loader; it never reaches a resolved config.

level.description: How much this project asks of itself: relaxed, standard, strict or pristine. A level is merged under everything written by hand, so it moves the defaults and never overrides a stated value.

locked.description: Only meaningful in a policy: the keys a project may not change.

overrides.description: Settings for a subtree, matched by glob against this file's directory. Read by the loader, which turns each entry into its own resolved config.

policy.description: A shared policy file, relative to this one, that every repository pointing at it inherits. Read by the loader; it never reaches a resolved config.

root.description: Stops the search for further config files above this one, for a repository checked out inside another one.

rule.description: Rules this project wrote, as `[[rule]]` blocks. The grammars are already in the binary; this is what lets a team ask a question rqx will never ship.
